title: Principal localization comparison for fixed degree-zero restriction data
statement: Let $S=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}S_n$ be a commutative graded ring and $M=\bigoplus_{z\in\mathbf Z}M_z$ an $S$-module with $S_nM_z\subset M_{n+z}$. Let $F=\{(f,d):d>0, f\in S_d\}$, $R_f=S_{(f)}$, $L_f=S_f$, $N_f=M_f$ [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero, def-weil-ring-localization-away, def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. Write $f\preceq g$ for a homogeneous relation $g^e=af$ with $e>0$. Suppose submodules $Z_f\subset N_f$ have precisely the equal-degree fractions as carriers [def-sc-degree-zero-module-fractions]. Suppose maps $\lambda_{f,g}:N_f\to N_g$, $\lambda^S_{f,g}:L_f\to L_g$, $\rho_{f,g}:Z_f\to Z_g$, $\rho^S_{f,g}:R_f\to R_g$ and $U_{f,g}=g^{\deg f}/f^{\deg g}$ are given. Assume $f/1$ is a unit with inverse $a/g^e$, multiplication by $f$ on $N_g$ is bijective, $\lambda$ is the unique $S$-linear extension of $x/1$ with formula $x/f^m\mapsto a^mx/g^{em}$, $\lambda^S$ preserves $S$, $\lambda$ is semilinear over $\lambda^S$, $\rho,\rho^S$ are their restrictions, $\rho$ is semilinear over $\rho^S$, and $\rho^S(U)$ is a unit. Then for every $f\preceq g$ there exist an additive equivalence $\theta:(Z_f)_{U_{f,g}}\cong Z_g$ and a ring equivalence $\theta^S:(R_f)_{U_{f,g}}\cong R_g$. They extend $\rho$ and $\rho^S$, satisfy $\rho^S(U)^k\theta(x/U^k)=\rho(x)$, and $\theta$ is semilinear over $\theta^S$. No coherence or existence of the input data is asserted.

proof.text: Apply the denominator-clearing and kernel-detection statements to each relation. Restrict scalars on Z g along rhoS and package rho as a linear map. The unit rhoS(U) and the clearing/kernel properties give IsLocalizedModule.Away via Mathlib IsLocalizedModule.Away.mk_of_addCommGroup. For the ring, the same properties give IsLocalization.Away, using subtraction to reduce equality to the zero kernel. IsLocalizedModule.iso and IsLocalization.algEquiv construct the equivalences. The unit fraction and algebraMap formulas give both extension laws. Apply linearity to U^k times x/U^k to obtain the fraction identity. For semilinearity, represent a scalar r by b/s, multiply both desired sides by the unit rhoS(s), and use linearity and the ring equivalence algebraMap formula to identify both with rhoS(b) times theta(x). Choose these uniquely specified comparisons for every relation.

theorem gradedModuleAwayComparison
    {S : Type u} [CommRing S] {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module S M]
    (𝒜 : ℕ → AddSubgroup S) [GradedRing 𝒜]
    (𝓜 : ℤ → AddSubgroup M) (h𝓜 : DirectSum.IsInternal 𝓜)
    (hsmul : ∀ (n : ℕ) (z : ℤ) (a : S) (x : M),
      a ∈ 𝒜 n → x ∈ 𝓜 z → a • x ∈ 𝓜 (n + z)) :
    let F := {p : S × ℕ // 0 < p.2 ∧ p.1 ∈ 𝒜 p.2}
    let R := fun f : F ↦ HomogeneousLocalization.Away 𝒜 f.val.1
    let L := fun f : F ↦ Localization.Away f.val.1
    let N := fun f : F ↦ LocalizedModule.Away f.val.1 M
    let Rel := fun f g : F ↦ ∃ (e k : ℕ) (a : S),
      0 < e ∧ a ∈ 𝒜 k ∧ g.val.1 ^ e = a * f.val.1
    letI : ∀ f : F, Module (R f) (N f) :=
      fun f ↦ Module.compHom (N f) (algebraMap (R f) (L f))
    ∀ (Z : ∀ f : F, Submodule (R f) (N f)),
      (∀ f : F, (Z f : Set (N f)) = degreeZeroFractions
        (fun n : ℕ ↦ (𝒜 n : Set S)) (fun n : ℕ ↦ (𝓜 n : Set M))
        (Submonoid.powers f.val.1)) →
    ∀ (lambda : ∀ (f g : F), Rel f g → N f →ₗ[S] N g)
      (lambdaS : ∀ (f g : F), Rel f g → L f →+* L g)
      (rho : ∀ (f g : F), Rel f g → Z f →+ Z g)
      (rhoS : ∀ (f g : F), Rel f g → R f →+* R g)
      (U : ∀ (f g : F), R f),
      (∀ (f g : F), (U f g).val = Localization.mk (g.val.1 ^ f.val.2)
        (⟨f.val.1 ^ g.val.2, ⟨g.val.2, rfl⟩⟩ : Submonoid.powers f.val.1)) ∧
      (∀ (f g : F) (p : Rel f g),
        IsUnit (algebraMap S (L g) f.val.1) ∧
        Function.Bijective (fun x : N g ↦ f.val.1 • x) ∧
        (∀ (e k : ℕ) (a : S), 0 < e → a ∈ 𝒜 k →
          g.val.1 ^ e = a * f.val.1 →
          algebraMap S (L g) f.val.1 * Localization.mk a
            (⟨g.val.1 ^ e, ⟨e, rfl⟩⟩ : Submonoid.powers g.val.1) = 1) ∧
        (∀ x : M, lambda f g p (mk x 1) = mk x 1) ∧
        (∀ T : N f →ₗ[S] N g,
          (∀ x : M, T (mk x 1) = mk x 1) → T = lambda f g p) ∧
        (∀ (e k : ℕ) (a : S), 0 < e → a ∈ 𝒜 k →
          g.val.1 ^ e = a * f.val.1 → ∀ (x : M) (m : ℕ),
          lambda f g p (mk x (⟨f.val.1 ^ m, ⟨m, rfl⟩⟩ : Submonoid.powers f.val.1)) =
            mk (a ^ m • x)
              (⟨g.val.1 ^ (e * m), ⟨e * m, rfl⟩⟩ : Submonoid.powers g.val.1)) ∧
        (∀ r : S, lambdaS f g p (algebraMap S (L f) r) = algebraMap S (L g) r) ∧
        (∀ (r : L f) (x : N f),
          lambda f g p (r • x) = lambdaS f g p r • lambda f g p x) ∧
        (∀ x : Z f, (rho f g p x : N g) = lambda f g p (x : N f)) ∧
        (∀ r : R f, (rhoS f g p r).val = lambdaS f g p r.val) ∧
        (∀ (r : R f) (x : Z f), rho f g p (r • x) = rhoS f g p r • rho f g p x) ∧
        IsUnit (rhoS f g p (U f g))) →
    ∃ (theta : ∀ (f g : F), Rel f g → LocalizedModule.Away (U f g) (Z f) ≃+ Z g)
      (thetaS : ∀ (f g : F), Rel f g → Localization.Away (U f g) ≃+* R g),
      (∀ (f g : F) (p : Rel f g),
        (∀ r : R f, thetaS f g p (algebraMap (R f) (Localization.Away (U f g)) r) =
          rhoS f g p r) ∧
        (∀ x : Z f, theta f g p (mk x 1) = rho f g p x) ∧
        (∀ (x : Z f) (k : ℕ), (rhoS f g p (U f g)) ^ k •
          theta f g p (mk x (⟨(U f g) ^ k, ⟨k, rfl⟩⟩ : Submonoid.powers (U f g))) =
            rho f g p x) ∧
        (∀ (r : Localization.Away (U f g)) (x : LocalizedModule.Away (U f g) (Z f)),
          theta f g p (r • x) = thetaS f g p r • theta f g p x))
